For the ninth day of the spring sale there are a few games that have been in a bunch of days, plus some older titles. I'm not going to cover all the games on sale, since they have a ton, but I'll pick some that I feel strongly about from each day.

Legend of Dungeon
This little dungeon crawler has a weird visual style that probably would have been better as plain 2D sidescrolling. You only shoot sideways anyway, so having to control the depth of your character to line up with the enemies is odd, and there isn't really anything in the game that is enhanced by having depth.

The premise is simple, fight your way to the lowest level of the dungeon, and then back up - although that could be quite challenging with the weird loot drops.

 

Dungeon Hearts
This is a match 3 game that looks like a rhythm game. It's a mobile port, and they didn't customize the controls for the PC - so while the game mechanics are solid it can be frustrating to actually play. Dragging and activating tiles are both controlled by your left mouse button, and the game is bad at differentiating which you meant to do - especially on fast levels.

 

Dungeon Defenders
There's actually a sequel for this game out now, but the original didn't thrill me. It has some towers but the actually killing usually comes down to the players - but in this case it just feels repetitive. I never felt a real sense of urgency or skill - like Sanctum 2 has - it's just flailing your sword or auto-shooting your wand. Since waves take a while this can become pretty monotonous.

 

Orborun
This is one of those ball/runner type games where you're navigating through an aerial obstacle course, trying to get a fast time and pick up some collectibles.

Unfortunately, the controls weren't tight and responsive enough for my taste - and it didn't have the constant fast pace I'd look for in a game like this. Your guy will actually unfurl out of his ball form and lumber along if you slow down too much.

That might not have been a deal-breaker for me, but there just wasn't anything else to make it a particularly unique or exceptional game, which is why I ended up not reviewing it. It wasn't bad, but it didn't strike me as particularly great either.

 

Super Meat Boy
Everyone should know this game by now - but if you don't, it's a good hardcore precision platformer. The controls are tight and feel satisfying, and the levels are challenging but fair. If you hit a spike or spinning saw blade you get sent back to the start, and once you finally complete the level you can watch all your ghosts go at once, in a flood of bloody explosions. It's very cathartic.

 

Bioshock Triple Pack
BioShock 1 is an FPS with a great atmosphere and unique environment, the only thing I really had an issue with were the big daddies - which were frustrating to fight.

Infinite had combat that was very similar to a normal FPS, and again had an interesting world. Additionally you get a brilliant AI companion, although mid-game it does start feeling a bit fetch-questish.

 

Shadow of Mordor
The gameplay in this was solid, with the overall collectibles and roaming feeling very much like Assassin's Creed. The combat was pretty easy - somewhat satisfying but would have been better if there was actually a chance of you dieing in a swarm of enemies. Currently you can just dash around and hop over dudes and be nearly invincible unless you mess up. Fun, but not difficult.

My video review is also based on the main game - there have been DLC that may have completed the story, but the main game itself kind of leaves you hanging.

 

Assassin's Creed 4: Black Flag
A lot of the land gameplay is very similar to other Assassin's Creed games, but the sailing in this game is fantastic - and I love all the scenes aboard ships. Those are what really set it apart from similar games and give it a great feel.
